standard.subject: Scaling Corvane’s AI inspection pilots after the Arden acquisition
standard.body:
Hi Elena,

Congratulations on closing the Arden Controls acquisition [[f1|and bringing the network to twelve plants]]. With [[f2|AI inspection pilots already running at Dayton and Greenville]], the next question is usually which pilots to scale first and what each plant needs in place before they do.

CGS helps manufacturers plan that first mile of AI adoption, from use-case sequencing to the operating model behind it. I would value 20 minutes to hear how you are approaching it, and I can share what we have seen work at similar manufacturers.

Would a short call in the week of 2 November suit you?

Best regards,
Alex Morgan
CGS Advisors

brief.subject: Twelve plants, two AI pilots: a quick question
brief.body:
Hi Elena,

[[f1|With Arden now part of Corvane]] and [[f2|inspection pilots live at Dayton and Greenville]], are you deciding which pilots to scale across the new network?

We help manufacturers plan exactly that step. Open to a 20-minute call the week of 2 November?

Alex Morgan, CGS Advisors

star.reply: Hi Alex, thanks for reaching out. Timing is good, as we are working through exactly this. Could we talk on Wednesday 4 November at 10:00 ET? Elena
star.note:
Call with Elena Fischer, 4 Nov 2026 (45 min). Elena brought her plant operations lead, Marco Silva.

Elena said the two AI inspection pilots "work in isolation, but we have no plan for scaling them across the twelve plants we now run after the Arden acquisition." Without a plan, each plant is choosing its own tools.

On outside help: "We'd rather bring in a partner for the first-mile plan than build it ourselves."

Elena owns the 2027 transformation budget; spend above $250K needs CEO sign-off, which she expects in January.

This would be Corvane's first project with CGS.

Agreed next step: a half-day scoping workshop on 24 November with her operations and IT leads. Marco will send the plant list before then.
